D007_m001.question:
I’ve been feeling really low for about seven months now. It’s not just stress from the office; it’s like this heavy sadness that doesn’t lift, even on weekends with my family. I used to be pretty organized at City Hall, but now I stare at files and just…don’t start. My wife says I move and talk slower, and I notice it too—getting dressed, walking to the bus, everything feels like wading through mud. Even when I sleep a full night, I wake up exhausted, like I didn’t sleep at all.

On top of that, for the last six months I’ve been convinced something is wrong inside my body—like my organs are rotting or rearranging themselves. Tests come back “normal,” but I’m sure they’re missing something. I also keep feeling things crawling or shifting under my skin, especially at night, but there’s nothing there. Sometimes my thoughts start linking by rhyme instead of sense—“time, crime, slime, climb”—and I catch myself talking like that at work, which is embarrassing. There was a stretch a couple of weeks where the body stuff and the crawling feelings were there even though my mood wasn’t quite as low, and that really scared me.
D007_m001.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m002.question:
I’ve been feeling really low for about seven months now. It’s like the bottom dropped out and never came back up. I used to joke with the kids on the bus and chat with the other drivers, but now I mostly keep to myself. On my days off, I just sit in my chair. I don’t return calls from my sister much anymore.

I wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning almost every day and just lie there, staring at the ceiling, feeling heavy. Even getting dressed or walking out to the bus feels like I’m moving through mud. The other drivers ask if I’m okay because I move so slow now.

For the past six months or so, I’ve also been noticing… strange things. Sometimes I smell smoke or chemicals on the bus or at home when no one else does. And I’m convinced the kids are talking about me in code, like their jokes or whispers are messages about how I’m doing my job. 

There were a couple of weeks when the sadness wasn’t as strong, but those smells and the feeling that people were sending me messages through little comments and TV shows were still there, and it really scared me.
D007_m002.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m003.question:
For about nine months now, I’ve felt like I’ve fallen out of my own life. It started with this heavy, numb feeling, like I’m hollowed out. I used to love chasing stories, arguing over edits, digging into leads; now I just… don’t care. I sleep 10–12 hours if I can, and on weekends I barely get out of bed. When I’m awake, I can’t sit still—pacing the apartment, rubbing my hands, picking at my skin while my husband tries to talk to me.

At the same time, something’s been off with how I see the world. Headlines, random tweets, even conversations in the newsroom feel like they’re aimed at me—like there’s a subtext everyone else understands. For a couple of weeks this spring, that was happening even when my mood wasn’t as low. I also keep feeling things crawling or brushing on my skin, especially at night, but there’s nothing there.

Sometimes when I’m trying to explain this, my words just fall apart—my sentences tangle up, and I can hear myself sounding messy and disconnected. It’s made it almost impossible to work, and my editor’s already cut back my assignments.
D007_m003.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m004.question:
It’s been going on maybe nine months now. I’d say the last seven months have been the worst. I just feel hollow most of the time, like there’s nothing inside. Stuff I used to enjoy—fishing on Sundays, watching games with my kids—doesn’t do anything for me anymore. After my shift, I just crash on the couch or in bed. I can sleep ten, twelve hours and still wake up exhausted, or I’ll nap in the middle of the day on my days off. When I am awake, I’m either pacing the house, rubbing my hands together, or picking at my arms without even noticing. My wife keeps telling me to sit still.

At the same time, I’ve had this strong sense that I’m meant for something huge, like I’ve got some kind of special influence over the machines at work, like they respond to me. Sometimes, even when I’m not eating, I get this weird metallic taste in my mouth, or like bitter chemicals. It’ll come out of nowhere. My wife says I sometimes use “my own words” that no one else understands when I’m trying to explain it. There was a stretch where the mood wasn’t as bad, but the special-power stuff and the strange tastes were still there. It’s gotten to the point where I’ve been missing shifts and my boss has warned me.
D007_m004.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m005.question:
It’s been about nine months now that things have been…off. The last seven months especially, I just feel flat. I get up around 3 or 4 a.m. every day and can’t fall back asleep. I used to like chatting with clients and grabbing drinks with my coworkers after work; now I don’t really care about any of it. Even with my kids on my weekends, I feel like I’m watching myself pretend to be their mom instead of actually feeling anything. I’m restless all the time—pacing around the apartment, picking at my fingers during calls, unable to sit still and finish paperwork, which has started to hurt my numbers at work.

On top of that, for about six months I’ve been completely convinced that one of our regional managers is secretly in love with me—there are “signs” everywhere: the way emails are worded, certain numbers in policy IDs. Sometimes, even when I’m not feeling especially low, I hear voices commenting on what I’m doing, usually just behind my left ear. When I try to explain all this, my thoughts get jumbled and the words come out wrong, like my sentences fall apart halfway through, and people look at me like they can’t follow what I’m saying.
D007_m005.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m006.question:
It’s been going on close to two years now. It started with feeling really low, and it just never lifted. I cry at the smallest things now—TV ads, someone raising their voice at work. I used to go fishing on Sundays, watch the game with the guys, but I just don’t care anymore. I mostly sit on the couch and eat; I’m constantly snacking, even when I’m not hungry. I’ve put on a lot of weight.  

I can’t shake this feeling that all of this is pointless anyway. I’m convinced something terrible is going to happen, like the world is slowly ending and I’m somehow responsible for it—like every mistake I make at the factory or at home is part of ruining everything. I feel like I deserve to be punished for it.  

Sometimes, even when I’m not eating, I suddenly taste metal or chemicals in my mouth, like poison. It makes me suspicious of food. My wife says I go off on these long rambles when she asks a simple question, and at work I can’t stay on track in meetings. It’s gotten hard to manage the line and people have noticed.
D007_m006.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m007.question:
I guess this all really started about a year and a half, almost two years ago. I’ve just felt low most days, like a heavy weight sitting on my chest. Things that used to matter at work—getting a floor done ahead of schedule, fixing a big problem before anyone noticed—now I just think, “What’s the point?” My wife says I’ve dropped a lot of weight, like 20 pounds in a month back then, but I wasn’t trying. I just didn’t care if I ate or not. Most days I feel like I’m useless, like everyone would be better off if I wasn’t around.

On top of that, for about a year and a few months I’ve been convinced people are watching me. Cameras in the vents at work, microphones in the light fixtures. I know it sounds strange, but it feels real. Sometimes I hear these voices, like two or three men arguing about me, calling me a “floorghost” or saying I’m “maintenance-broken.” Those are my words for it—no one else uses them. Even when my mood isn’t at its worst, the voices and the feeling of being watched still hang around. It’s gotten hard to manage my crew or even show up some days.
D007_m007.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m008.question:
It’s been going on close to two years now. I first noticed feeling really down about a year and a half ago. I used to love teaching my students and practicing for hours, but now I just stare at the piano and feel…blank. I cancel lessons, fall behind on simple things like answering messages. I’ve put on a lot of weight in just a few weeks at one point, which makes me feel even worse about myself. I cry at the smallest things—commercials, a wrong note, my husband being five minutes late. I keep thinking I ruin everything for everyone, that I’m a burden and deserve whatever bad happens.

On top of that, for about the last year and four months, I’ve become convinced there’s something seriously wrong inside my body—like my organs are rotting or twisted. Tests come back “normal,” but I can’t shake it. I sometimes smell this awful, rotten odor that no one else seems to notice, like something decomposing inside me. There were a couple of weeks when that was happening even though my mood wasn’t as low, and my thoughts jump around when I try to explain it—like my mind can’t stay on one track.
D007_m008.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m009.question:
I plan weddings for a living, so I’m used to stress, but this is different. For about a year and a half I’ve felt…hollow, like there’s nothing inside. Things that used to excite me—designing a reception, seeing a bride cry happy tears—now feel flat. I mostly go through the motions. My appetite’s dropped a lot; some days I’ll realize it’s 4 p.m. and I’ve barely eaten. 

I keep thinking I ruin everything. If a centerpiece is crooked or it rains on someone’s day, I’m convinced it’s somehow my fault, like I deserve to be punished for it. It’s gotten hard to keep up with clients; I’ve cut back on bookings because I just can’t cope.

On top of that, for a bit over a year I’ve been absolutely sure I have this special influence over people, like I can make their futures turn out a certain way just by planning their wedding. Sometimes I feel things crawling or brushing on my skin when nothing’s there. My husband says I sometimes use strange words that don’t exist, but they make perfect sense to me at the time.
D007_m009.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m010.question:
I’ve been feeling like this for almost two years now. It started with feeling low and just got worse. I cry at the stupidest things, like an advert on TV or if my kids spill something. I used to be solid, you know, reliable. Now I can barely drag myself to work, and on my days off I just sit in the chair staring at the wall. I’m putting things off at the site, too, which is dangerous in my line of work.

I’ve put on a lot of weight over a month or so, just eating without really being hungry. I feel useless, like my family would be better off without me.  

Around a year and a bit ago, I started getting these strange tastes in my mouth, like metal or chemicals, even when I’m not eating. Sometimes I call it “mouth-buzzing” and “flavor ghosts”—my wife says those aren’t real words.  

I’ve become convinced my wife’s cheating on me, even though I can’t prove it. If she’s late from the shops, I “know” she’s lying. That thought sticks, even in weeks when my mood isn’t as bad.
D007_m010.options:
A. Schizophrenia
    B. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    C. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m011.question:
It’s been about a year since things really started to go off. The last seven months have been the worst, with everything sort of happening at once.

I’m a UI/UX designer, so I’m used to being detail‑oriented, but now I can’t even get myself to open Figma most days. I just sit there, staring, unable to start anything. I used to love sketching interfaces and doing little side projects; now I don’t care about any of it. At the same time, I’m constantly on edge—pacing around the apartment, picking at my skin, wringing my hands. I can’t sit still, but I also can’t actually do anything.

I’m convinced there’s something rotting inside me—my organs feel wrong, like they’re decaying. Sometimes I smell this horrible, sickly sweet, almost “rotted meat” kind of odor, even when my husband says there’s nothing there. I catch myself standing or holding my arms in weird positions for long stretches without noticing.

My thoughts and speech get jumbled; my husband says I start talking in fragments that don’t make sense. I feel like everything that’s gone wrong—with work, with our marriage—is my fault, like I deserve to be punished. I’ve thought through a very specific way to end my life—where I’d go, what I’d use. There were a couple of weeks earlier this year when the low mood lifted a bit, but the beliefs about my body and the smells were still there, just as strong.
D007_m011.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007_m012.question:
I guess this really started about a year ago, but it’s been a lot worse these past seven months. I used to be pretty social at the café and go out after shifts, but now I mostly just go straight home and ignore my friends’ texts. I don’t really care about anything I used to like—music, drawing, even watching dumb shows just feels pointless.

Most days I’m restless and can’t sit still. On my breaks I pace behind the shop or pick at my skin until it hurts. I keep thinking I’m useless, like I’m just taking up space and everyone would be better off without me. At night I lie there wishing I just wouldn’t wake up, not planning anything, just… wanting it to stop.

I’m also really convinced something terrible is coming, like the world is sort of rotting from the inside and going to end soon. Sometimes my coffee tastes like metal or chemicals, even when I made it myself and nobody else notices. My coworkers say I talk “all over the place,” like my thoughts jump around. I catch myself making stupid jokes or acting kind of goofy at work at totally wrong times, even when I feel awful inside.
D007_m012.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007_m013.question:
I guess this really started about a year ago, but it’s been much worse these last seven months. I’m a wedding photographer, so I’m always around people, but lately I just… avoid everyone. I stopped going out with friends, I let messages pile up, even family group chats feel like too much. I mostly sit at home on the couch, moving slow, like my body’s made of concrete. Even walking to the kitchen feels like a chore.  

On shoots, I can’t focus. I’ll start talking about the flowers and then suddenly I’m rambling about something random that pops in my head, and it doesn’t really connect. Sometimes I catch myself making weird faces without meaning to. I feel like I’m useless, like my work is terrible and my husband would be better off without me. I go to bed thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up.  

I keep feeling little crawling sensations on my skin, like bugs, but there’s nothing there. And I’m convinced people are talking about me—like song lyrics at weddings or guests’ whispers are secretly about me. Even when my mood dipped a bit less for a couple weeks, those things were still happening.
D007_m013.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007_m014.question:
It’s been about a year since things started feeling… off. At first it was just this fixed feeling that something terrible was coming, like the world is quietly winding down. It doesn’t feel like a worry; it feels like a fact, like everything around me is already kind of… cancelled.

For the last seven months or so, it’s gotten much worse. I used to love working on app flows and doing little illustration side projects, but now I can’t make myself open Figma unless someone’s chasing me for a deadline. Even then I just sit there, staring. My body feels slowed down, like I’m moving through glue. My husband notices I shuffle around the apartment and just sit in one spot for ages.

Sometimes I suddenly taste metal or chemicals in my mouth when there’s nothing there. I’ve caught myself copying other people’s movements in meetings without meaning to, like mirroring their hand gestures exactly. I also make up “shortcut words” when I talk—“gridfog,” “color-sinking”—and everyone looks confused, but they make sense to me in the moment.

I’m constantly replaying tiny things I’ve said or done, feeling like I’ve ruined everything. A few times, walking over a bridge or waiting for the metro, I’ve had this sharp pull to just step off or into the train. It scares me, but part of me thinks it wouldn’t matter, since everything’s ending anyway.
D007_m014.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007_m015.question:
It’s been about a year since things really started to go off. For the last seven months or so, it’s like two tracks running at once. On one hand, I feel… special, I guess. I keep thinking I have this unique “edit-sight,” like I can bend time in the footage in a way no one else can, that directors will eventually realize I’m the real author of their films. I know it sounds weird, but it feels absolutely true in the moment. I even catch myself using these little “code words” I’ve made up when I’m trying to explain my ideas, and then people just stare at me.

I also keep smelling this burnt plastic or chemical odor, especially when I’m alone at the studio, but no one else notices it. Sometimes, when I’m stressed at the workstation, my hands just repeat the same little tapping motion on the desk for minutes; I don’t even realize I’m doing it.

At the same time, I’ve slowed down so much. Even walking to the kitchen feels heavy. I barely care about work anymore—even when a cut turns out great, it means nothing. I keep replaying tiny mistakes from years ago, obsessing over how I ruined everything. Most nights I lie in bed thinking it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up—not with a plan, just this constant “I don’t want to be here” looping in my head. It’s gotten hard to keep up with deadlines, and I’ve started turning down projects because I just can’t make myself care.
D007_m015.options:
A. Major Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)

D007_m016.question:
I guess this really started about a year ago. Around ten months back my mood just dropped and never really came back up. I feel low pretty much all day, every day. I used to love flying and even the pre‑flight checks, but now it all feels pointless. I’ve been calling in sick more, letting my co‑pilot handle things I’d normally do myself. Even simple stuff at home—paying bills, fixing little things—just sits there. I just can’t get myself to start.

My appetite’s gone; my wife keeps telling me I’m losing weight. I wake up around 3 or 4 a.m. most mornings with this heavy feeling in my chest and can’t fall back asleep. Physically I feel wiped out, like I’ve already flown a long-haul before I even get out of bed.

For about eight months I’ve been convinced something terrible is coming, like the world’s on a countdown and no one else sees it. Sometimes I hear this male voice, kind of behind me, saying things like “It’s already over” or “Why bother?” That’s happened even during stretches when I didn’t feel quite as down, which scares me.
D007_m016.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m017.question:
It’s been about a year now that things have felt…wrong. The low mood started first, around ten months ago. At first I thought it was just burnout from wedding season, but it never lifted. I feel sort of empty most of the time, like someone turned the volume down on all my emotions. Brides come in crying with joy and I just stand there, going through the motions, pretending to care.

I’m exhausted constantly—just pinning a hem or standing through a fitting makes my body feel heavy, like I’m wading through water. I barely eat; food just doesn’t appeal to me anymore, and most days I have to remind myself to put anything in my mouth. Sleep is broken—I fall asleep okay, then wake up at 2 or 3 a.m. for no reason and just lie there, staring at the ceiling.

For the past eight months, I’ve also had this fixed feeling that everything is heading toward some kind of collapse, like the world is quietly winding down and we’re all pretending it’s not happening. Sometimes I suddenly taste metal or something rotten in my mouth when there’s nothing there—it makes me wonder if it’s a sign of that coming disaster. On some days, even when I don’t feel especially sad, that sense that everything is ending is still there. I’ve stopped sketching new designs, stopped seeing friends. It all feels pointless and I can’t make myself care enough to do anything more than the bare minimum.
D007_m017.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m018.question:

I’m convinced something terrible is coming, like the world is rotting from the inside and about to collapse. Even on weeks when my mood wasn’t quite as low, those visions and that feeling that everything’s ending never really went away.

A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m021.question:
It’s been going on close to two years now. It really started about a year and a half ago with this heavy, constant low mood. I feel like I’m moving through mud—at work on the ward I walk slower, even hanging IV bags feels like a chore. I’m just… flat. There was never anything solid, but I still check his socials, reread old messages, and I can’t shake the certainty. Sometimes I feel things crawling on my skin, like bugs under my scrubs, but when I look there’s nothing there.

At times I just shut down when people ask me to do things—charge nurse, friends, my mom—I either say nothing or do the opposite without really knowing why. It’s starting to affect my work; I’ve cut my hours and call in sick more because I just can’t cope.
D007_m021.options:

    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m022.question:
It’s been about two years now since things started feeling… off. It began not long after my husband died. Around that time I became convinced he’d been seeing someone else, even though I never found anything concrete. I keep going over old texts, old receipts, replaying conversations, and I can’t shake the idea that he betrayed me. My sister and my son say I’m “fixated,” but it feels absolutely certain to me.

For the last year and a half I’ve been low most days—heavy, flat. I wake up around 3 or 4 a.m. and just stare at the ceiling, unable to fall back asleep. When people talk to me, I lose track and go off on other things; I see their faces waiting for an answer, and sometimes I just don’t have much to say at all. Occasionally I even catch myself copying someone’s gestures without meaning to.
D007_m022.options:
A. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features

D007_m023.question:
I guess the main thing is that I just haven’t felt like myself for almost two years now. I’ve been really down most of the time, like there’s this heaviness that doesn’t really lift. I used to love going out with friends, planning campaigns, networking, but for the last year and a half I’ve mostly been avoiding people outside of work. Even online, I just… lurk. I don’t really engage.

There’s also this whole thing with my ex. I was completely convinced she was cheating on me, checking her socials nonstop, rereading comments, looking for hidden meaning. There were a couple of weeks when that suspiciousness and the strange smells were there even though my mood wasn’t especially low, which frightened me even more.

It’s been a little over two years now that I’ve felt like I’m coming apart. For almost two years I’ve been down pretty much every day—this heavy, flat kind of sadness. I used to be able to grind 14-hour days on the startup; now I just pace around the office or my apartment, wearing a path in the floor, picking at my fingers, unable to sit still long enough to answer an email. My focus is shot—people talk to me about runway or investors and halfway through I lose the thread, drift off, or my mind jumps sideways.

Around a year and a half ago, other things started. I sometimes smell this sharp, chemical-burn kind of odor, or like something rotting, even when no one else notices anything. It’ll follow me from room to room. My team will ask a simple question and I catch myself going off on these long explanations about unrelated stuff—competitors, my ex, random connections—and then realize I never actually answered.

I’m convinced my ex is seeing someone else and lying about it, even though I have nothing concrete. I’ve spent nights scrolling through her socials, dissecting every like and comment. It’s wrecked my ability to run the company, and honestly, my life feels like it’s been on pause since this all started.

D007_m049.question:
It’s been a little over two years since this started messing with my life. I used to be a solid patrol cop—night shifts, paperwork, court—no problem. Now I’m barely keeping it together.

For almost two years I’ve felt…blank. Not sad exactly, just like everything’s turned down low. My mom jokes, tries to get a rise out of me, and I just sit there, nothing. Talking feels like wading through mud. When people ask me something, it takes me a while to answer, like my brain has to boot up. At work briefings I lose track halfway through sentences, miss radio calls, can’t follow simple instructions. I’ve had to call in sick a lot, and they’ve pulled me off the street more than once.

The weird part is my body. I keep feeling things crawling under my skin, especially on my arms and back, like bugs or wires moving. I’m convinced something’s wrong inside me—like my organs are rotting or someone’s put something in me—but every test comes back “normal.” Sometimes my thoughts and words get so jumbled even I can’t follow what I’m saying, and that scares me more than anything.
